body: T18 - FOCUS LOSS REDESIGN. HIGHEST ADHD FOCUS DROP MOMENT IN MCM: The transition between submitting an exam and reading the score. Current: submit -> instant score display -> Kai must scroll up to read from start. Focus drops because there is no momentum. He submitted, something happened, now he has to hunt for the result. BEFORE: user clicks submit, page reloads with score at bottom or middle of page, browser scroll position is unpredictable. Kai sees a changed page but does not know where to look. AFTER: On gradeExam() completion: smooth scroll to top of score section (behavior:smooth 200ms). Score section reveals with phase 2 animation (600ms). First item visible after scroll is the score percentage, then grade letter, then per-question results below. This creates a momentum chain: submit, scroll-up, score-appears, read. Each step has a visual cue for what comes next. WHY THIS IS THE HIGHEST DROP MOMENT: After submit Kai has done the work. His engagement has peaked. Any friction between submit and reward is where ADHD loses the thread. The current page-level scroll confusion is that friction. The redesign: one scroll, one animation, score is the first thing he sees. SPEC FOR GA: after gradeExam() runs, before showing score, call scoreSection.scrollIntoView({behavior:smooth,block:start}). Then trigger phase 2 animation. No other scroll happens. Score section is always the first visible thing post-submit.
